summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, and tracheostomy dependence was admitted from a long-term facility for fever, tachypnea, and hypotension. Initial concern was for pneumonia, but urine culture revealed Pseudomonas aeruginosa with over 100,000 organisms/mL, leading to a diagnosis of pseudomonal urosepsis. He was treated with IV Zosyn for 8 days, guided by sensitivities. Respiratory symptoms were attributed to chronic interstitial lung disease and improved with supportive care. Oral vancomycin was continued for C. diff prophylaxis. A midline was used for IV access and removed before discharge. He stabilized clinically, completed therapy, and was discharged to extended care with plans for orthopedic follow-up and medication continuation.
